# beenfar_device (Resource)

A device adopted by the controller. Creating it adopts the device, which must have contacted the controller (it is then listed by `beenfar_pending_devices`); destroying it forgets the device.

A device that was factory reset comes back awaiting re-adoption. Terraform then plans to create the resource again, and applying accepts the re-adoption: the device keeps its id and its switch port settings. Creating the resource for a device that is already adopted fails; import it instead (by id or MAC).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Adopts the device once it has contacted the controller (for UniFi, after
# it was pointed at http://<controller>:8080/inform).
resource "beenfar_device" "core_switch" {
  mac             = "f0:9f:c2:79:63:90"
  wait_for_device = "5m"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mac` (String) MAC address, lower case and colon-separated (`aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`).

### Optional

- `wait_for_device` (String) How long create waits for the device to contact the controller, as a Go duration (e.g. `5m`). Unset or `0s`: the device must already be known.

### Read-Only

- `adapter` (String) Adapter that manages the device, e.g. `unifi`.
- `firmware` (String) Firmware version the device reported.
- `id` (String) Server-assigned identifier. Import uses it.
- `ip` (String) IP address the device reported.
- `model` (String) Model the device reported.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an adopted device by id or MAC address.
terraform import beenfar_device.example f0:9f:c2:79:63:90
```
